brief: 5 things that actually close enterprise deals — from a 7-figure sales leader.

slots.author: Marcus Chen
slots.headline: 5 Things That Actually Close Enterprise Deals
slots.body: Most reps chase activity. Top reps build trust, align stakeholders, and engineer consensus. Here are 5 moves that actually win.

slots.author: Marcus Chen
slots.title: Champion a Power Sponsor
slots.body: Find the executive with budget authority and a burning pain. Coach them to sell internally. No champion, no deal.

slots.author: Marcus Chen
slots.title: Map the Buying Committee
slots.body: Enterprise decisions have 6–10 stakeholders. Map each influencer, blocker, and gatekeeper. Then build a plan to win every vote.

slots.author: Marcus Chen
slots.title: Quantify ROI Early
slots.body: Buyers need business case ammo for finance. Show exact cost of inaction and projected ROI in their language, not yours.

slots.author: Marcus Chen
slots.title: Co-Create the Evaluation
slots.body: Don't pitch; architect the criteria with the buyer. When your solution defines the rubric, competitors become checked boxes.

slots.author: Marcus Chen
slots.title: Secure Mutual Action Plans
slots.body: Replace vague follow-ups with signed milestones. A mutual close plan creates accountability and exposes red flags before they kill the deal.

slots.author: Marcus Chen
slots.title: Remove Risk Before Closing
slots.body: Enterprise buyers fear career risk more than price. Offer pilots, phased rollouts, and escape clauses to make saying yes safe.

slots.author: Marcus Chen
slots.headline: What's Your Best Enterprise Closing Move?
slots.body: Drop your #1 deal-closing tactic in the comments. I'd love to steal your playbook.
